newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber ends up sharply to limit, new highs set.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber ends up sharply to limit, new highs set.

text.p: CME lumber ended up sharply to the $10.00 per tbf daily limit as technical buying and support from expected increased product demand combined to boost prices in a shortened pre-holiday session, traders said.
March Lumber finished up the daily limit at $425.50 per tbf and and May ended up $9.00 at $395.50 after being up the limit earlier. Other months ended mostly up $7.10 to $3.20.

Ideas demand for lumber will increase next week as a warming trend takes over from bitter cold added to carryover technical buying to push futures through another chart point and touch off buy stops, traders said.
"There is anticipation the weather is going to improve next week and maybe retail demand and pricing is going to improve," said Neil Schmaedick, Forest Products analyst for Smith Barney.
Schmaedick said he has not seen any improvement in cash as yet but expected cash prices to be higher next week.
Random Lengths quoted cash spruce at $396, off $4 from midweek and $14 under last Friday's level. Poor weather conditions had cut demand for wood recently, they said.
Futures closed at noon ahead of the Martin Luther King Jr. holiday on Monday. Lumber will also close early Monday.
